req.title: Create form GET returns 200
req.statement: The system shall serve the create-post form at GET /create for authenticated users.

doc.reasoning: The requirement states that GET /create must return HTTP 200 for authenticated users. Three test cases are designed: (1) positive — authenticated user gets 200 and the create form HTML; (2) negative — unauthenticated user is redirected (302) not served the form; (3) boundary — the state transition from unauthenticated to authenticated (session boundary) yields exactly 200. Each test is self-contained, uses the in-process Flask test client, pre-loaded fixture credentials (user 'test'/'test'), and asserts exact values to maximise mutation kill rate.

tests.name: test_create_get_authenticated_returns_200
preconditions: App is initialised with TESTING=True and a fresh temp database
Database contains fixture user id=1 username='test' password='test'
User 'test' is logged in via POST /auth/login
expected: Response body contains the create-post form HTML
trace: R-FLASKR-038: GET /create for authenticated user must return 200
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

def test_create_get_authenticated_returns_200():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    login_resp = client.post(
        '/auth/login',
        data={'username': 'test', 'password': 'test'}
    )
    assert login_resp.status_code == 302
    resp = client.get('/create')
    assert resp.status_code == 200
    assert b'<form' in resp.data

test_create_get_authenticated_returns_200()

tests.name: test_create_get_after_login_then_logout_returns_302
preconditions: App is initialised with TESTING=True and a fresh temp database
Database contains fixture user id=1 username='test' password='test'
User 'test' logs in, then logs out — session transitions from authenticated to anonymous
trace: R-FLASKR-038: state boundary between authenticated (200) and unauthenticated (302) must be exact
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

def test_create_get_after_login_then_logout_returns_302():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    login_resp = client.post(
        '/auth/login',
        data={'username': 'test', 'password': 'test'}
    )
    assert login_resp.status_code == 302
    resp_auth = client.get('/create')
    assert resp_auth.status_code == 200
    logout_resp = client.get('/auth/logout')
    assert logout_resp.status_code == 302
    resp_anon = client.get('/create')
    assert resp_anon.status_code == 302
    assert resp_anon.status_code != 200
    assert '/auth/login' in resp_anon.headers['Location']

test_create_get_after_login_then_logout_returns_302()

import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

def test_create_get_response_body_contains_form_fields():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'test', 'password': 'test'})
    resp = client.get('/create')
    assert resp.status_code == 200
    assert b'title' in resp.data
    assert b'body' in resp.data
    assert b'<form' in resp.data
    assert b'submit' in resp.data.lower() or b'Save' in resp.data

tests.name: test_create_get_wrong_credentials_cannot_access_form
preconditions: App is initialised with TESTING=True and a fresh temp database
Database contains fixture user id=1 username='test' password='test'
Login attempt with wrong password fails — session remains unauthenticated
expected: Login POST returns 200 (form re-rendered with error, not redirect)
trace: R-FLASKR-038: failed login leaves user unauthenticated; GET /create must not return 200
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

def test_create_get_wrong_credentials_cannot_access_form():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    bad_login = client.post(
        '/auth/login',
        data={'username': 'test', 'password': 'wrongpassword'}
    )
    assert bad_login.status_code == 200
    assert b'Incorrect password.' in bad_login.data
    resp = client.get('/create')
    assert resp.status_code == 302
    assert resp.status_code != 200
    assert '/auth/login' in resp.headers['Location']

test_create_get_wrong_credentials_cannot_access_form()
